subject: Pilot model shortlist, context constraints & onboarding milestones
messages:
From: Patrick O'Neill <patrick@datasage.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope and quick ask: model guidance + token estimate

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow up from our product / infra team: before we lock the pilot start date they want a short list of models you recommend for our primary flows and a rough monthly token estimate so they can size networking/GPU egress and budget.

A very short description of our footprint:
- Product: Document-to-chat for enterprise customers (legal, HR, contracts).
- Typical user flow: upload 20–100 documents per customer, vector search + 1–3 follow-up clarifying Qs, then a final generation (summary / clause extraction).
- Expectation for pilot: 10 customers, ~5k active users total across customers, average 2.5 queries/user/day.

Can you propose 2–3 model candidates (tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs context length) and a ballpark monthly token calc we can show procurement? Also attaching the pilot scope PDF and a link to a small sample corpus.

Attached: datasheet-pilot-scope.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-sample-docs

Best,
Patrick
Product Ops — DataSage

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick O'Neill <patrick@datasage.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and quick ask: model guidance + token estimate

Hi Patrick —

Appreciate the summary — this is the exact level of detail we need to lock the pilot. Below is a shortlist oriented to your retrieval + doc-chat workload, with recommended context length and a conservative monthly token estimate. I also attached a one-sheet that lists the pilot requirements and what we'll need to run initial benchmarks.

Model shortlist (tradeoffs):
- Redwood-Instruct-13B (recommended starter) — 4k context, strong instruction-following, lower latency vs 70B, good balance of cost and accuracy for Q/A and clause extraction.
- Llama-3-70B-q4 (high-context option) — 32k context good for whole-document prompts and long-form synthesis; higher latency and cost but reduces retrieval/concat complexity.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (throughput option) — 6k context, best cost/throughput for high qps, slightly lower on complex legal reasoning but excellent for summarization when paired with retrieval.

Conservative token estimate (pilot: 10 customers, 5k active users, 2.5 queries/user/day):
- Queries/day = 5,000 * 2.5 = 12,500 queries/day
- Avg tokens per query (prompt + retrieval context + response): assume prompt 450, retrieval context 1,100, response 600 => ~2,150 tokens/query
- Daily tokens = 12,500 * 2,150 = ~26.9M tokens/day
- Monthly (30d) = ~806M tokens/month

Sizing notes:
- If using Llama-3-70B with 32k context, average retrieval tokens might fall (fewer calls) but response tokens could increase; plan +/− 20% variance.
- With caching + batching we typically see 15–25% token savings for repetitive queries across a tenant.

Next steps / asks from DataSage:
1) Grant us access to the sample corpus in Drive (link above) so our bench team can run representative prompts.
2) Confirm pilot start week (we propose 2026-06-14).
3) Share any compliance constraints (data retention, redaction) so we pick an appropriate model hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated).

Attached: redwood_pilot_requirements.xlsx

If this looks good I'll loop in the bench engineer to schedule a short (1 hour) run and share a preliminary cost/throughput snapshot.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, patrick@datasage.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and quick ask: model guidance + token estimate

Thanks Patrick + Evelyn — quick ops note from infra/serving side.

Two engineering points to consider when picking between the 13B vs 70B path:
- Prefix/KV cache: for a retrieval-heavy workflow we should enable KV caching at the route level. That reduces repeated autoregressive decode for identical context prefixes (we've seen 20–40% token reduction in pilot runs).
- Warm-start / windowing: If you can accept modest truncation (summaries + extracted spans) we can keep peak context at ~8k for most queries and use retrieval to stitch in long context only for edge cases. That makes the 13B and 7B options much more cost-effective.

Operational ask: please include a representative set of long documents (one or two contracts ~20–40 pages) in the sample data so we can validate latency with 8k vs 32k prompts.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, patrick@datasage.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and quick ask: model guidance + token estimate

Adding a quick cost/throughput perspective. High-level recommendations for the pilot: start with Redwood-Instruct-13B on q4_8 quant (or q4_m if you want slightly better quality) and run the following knobs during bench:
- batch_size = 8 for tail-latency control
- enable continuous batching on the route to coalesce small requests
- token budget guardrails: 4k prompt cap, 1.5k response cap in initial pilot to avoid runaway costs

I've attached a simple estimator CSV with per-token cost assumptions and throughput numbers for single-GPU 13B / 70B. If the bench confirms latency is acceptable we can prototype a 32k path for a subset of customers.

Attachment: cost_estimator_v1.csv

—Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
